history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Searched for: hamster dance origins tempo lyrics licensing creator; rooster disney song rooster narrator. Findings:
- The Hampsterdance: Originated as a 1998 web page created by Deidre LaCarte featuring animated hamsters and sped‑up audio. Commercial single “The Hampsterdance Song” was produced by the Boomtang Boys and often credited under “Hampton the Hampster.” It uses a sped‑up sample/melody from Disney’s Robin Hood.
- Tempo/Lyrics: The hamster single is faster and includes novelty lyrics not present in the original film cue; the rooster film version is slower and mostly a wordless scat-style motif.
- Credits/Ownership: Public-facing credits frequently highlight Deidre LaCarte (site creator) and Hampton the Hampster persona for the viral phenomenon; the commercial track credits Boomtang Boys as producers. The underlying melody in Robin Hood is titled “Whistle Stop,” composed for the film. The on-screen rooster (Alan-a-Dale) performs it in the movie.
- Rooster details: The rooster character in Disney’s Robin Hood performs the theme; composition attribution in film materials is to the songwriter for that cue.
Summary: For the hamster release, public-facing attribution often centers on Deidre LaCarte (creator of the original hamster website), Hampton the Hampster (character), and the Boomtang Boys (producers). The underlying tune originates from the Robin Hood rooster performance.
